LESSON: MIXTURES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
Strand: Mixtures, Elements, and Compounds
Topic 2.1: Mixtures
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 18

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Mixtures, part of Mixtures, Elements, and Compounds in Grade 7 INTEGRATED SCIENCE.

Key inquiry question: How is the separation of mixtures important in day-to-day life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. collaboratively categorise the mixtures as homogeneous or heterogeneous,

2. discuss the meaning of the terms solvent, solute, and solution,

3. share tasks as they carry out activities to separate homogeneous mixtures,

4. discuss the applications of separating mixtures in day-to-day life,

5. use digital or print media to search for more information on fraction distillation as a method of separating a mixture.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. collaboratively categorise the mixtures as homogeneous or heterogeneous,
2. discuss the meaning of the terms solvent, solute, and solution,
3. share tasks as they carry out activities to separate homogeneous mixtures,
4. discuss the applications of separating mixtures in day-to-day life,
5. use digital or print media to search for more information on fraction distillation as a method of separating a mixture.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Mixtures together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: the learner learns data presentation as they work collaboratively to categorise the

mixtures as homogeneous or heterogeneous.

• Learning to Learn: the learner learns how to separate various mixtures as they carry out activities to separate homogeneous

mixtures.

Values:
Unity: the learner works harmoniously with peers while carrying out activities to separate homogeneous mixtures.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
Peer Education and Mentorship: the leaner practises sharing of tasks as they carry out activities to separate homogeneous

mixtures.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can relate methods of separating mixtures in cereals to heterogeneous mixtures in Agriculture.
